A statement runs from its heading to the last line before the first upright-roman prose line, 'Proof', or the next heading, read from the PDF's fonts with pdfminer.six 20260107 (theorem bodies are set in italic); every boundary was reviewed, and two were cut by hand at the stated text. manuscripts.title: Sharp nodal length on smooth surfaces

candidates.label: Theorem 1.1
candidates.heading: Theorem 1.1.
candidates.statement: Let (M, g) be a closed connected C∞ Riemannian surface. There is a finite constant C = C(M, g) such that every nonzero real Laplace eigenfunction satisfying −Δgu = λu, λ > 0, obeys H1 g(Zu) ≤ C √ λ. Here H1 g is Hausdorff measure for the Riemannian distance. The same constant applies to every eigenfunction in every positive eigenspace.

Assume Sj −→ ∞, Kj Dj −→ 0, sup j ∥pj∥∞ < ∞, K2 j ∥∇pj∥∞ SjDj −→ 0. (2.2) Local versions of the coefficient assumptions on relatively compact subdisks suffice. For positive constants cj, suppose the measures dμj = cje−2Bj·x |Uj(x)|2 dx have mass at most one on Ω. Every upper semicontinuous logarithmic profile with the compact, open, and weighted bounds of Lemma 2.1 is subharmonic on Ω, with the identically −∞ function allowed.

candidates.heading: Proposition 3.15 (Topological transfer of trace budgets).
candidates.statement: Fix generic trace data as in Lemma 3.11 and a sufficiently fine generic mesh from Lemma 3.12. There is an onto locally bi-Lipschitz homeomorphism H0 : Ω → Ω′, locally specified by finitely many C1 formulas on closed pieces, whose image lengths and areas on the measured traces are at most their tie budgets plus arbitrarily small prescribed local errors. Nonnegative continuous output weights are allowed, with the simplex- supremum budgets of Definition 3.13. The map can be arbitrarily close to f, with reciprocal closeness on interior compact sets, within the mesh displacement and chosen local modification errors. It can retain smaller exact affine germs previously installed at a locally finite family of crossings and finitely many star centers, and can retain strict compact forward and inverse safety conditions, including angular cone conditions, whenever they have positive margins. For this relative usage, measured data are separated from buffered open exemptions around the protected germs: a measured trace either avoids the exempt cores, or its weight vanishes there with a buffer. Every germ required to remain exact in H0 is contained in one of these buffered exemptions. The affine crossing germs installed at the newly cleaned measured hits are retained only in the intermediate map G for the concentration calculation; no affine-germ condition at those hits is imposed on T ◦G. The mesh and all measured configurations are fixed before the squeezing floors are selected.

candidates.label: Theorem 4.1
candidates.name: Low-exponent approximation
candidates.heading: Theorem 4.1 (Low-exponent approximation).
candidates.statement: Let Ω, Ω′ ⊂ R3 be bounded domains, let 1 ≤ p ≤ 2, and let f : Ω → Ω′ be a homeomorphism in W1,p(Ω; R3). For every ε > 0 there is a locally bi-Lipschitz homeomorphism H : Ω → Ω′ such that Z Ω |H − f|p + |DH − Df|p < ε. (4.1) In particular, the target of H is exactly Ω′, and H ∈ W1,p(Ω; R3).

manuscripts.title: Strong diffeomorphic approximation in three dimensions for p>2

candidates.label: Theorem 1.1
candidates.heading: Theorem 1.1.
candidates.statement: Let Ω, Λ ⊂ R3 be bounded domains, let 2 < p < ∞, and let f : Ω → Λ be a homeomorphism in W1,p(Ω; R3). There exist C∞ diffeomorphisms fj : Ω → Λ, each belonging to W1,p(Ω; R3), such that Z Ω |fj − f|p + |Dfj − Df|p dx −→ 0. (1.1)

candidates.label: Proposition 2.6
candidates.name: Target flattening
candidates.heading: Proposition 2.6 (Target flattening).
candidates.statement: Given ε > 0, 0 < λ < 1/100, and a positive continuous fine tolerance a on Λ, one can retain a compact set K ⊂ D with µ(D \ K) < ε and construct a Lipschitz map S0 : Λ → Λ with the following properties. 1. The map is the identity outside finitely many disjoint rectangular boxes compactly contained in Λ, Lip(S0) ≤ C, and |S0(y) − y| < a(y). The constant C is absolute. For 0 < κ ≤ 1, Sκ = (1 − κ)S0 + κ id is a bi-Lipschitz homeomorphism of Λ onto itself. 2. With Fκ = Sκ ◦ f for 0 ≤ κ ≤ 1, |DFκ| ≤ C|Df| a.e. on Ω, |DFκ − Df| ≤ Cλ|Df| a.e. on K. (2.7) Moreover, Fκ → F0 strongly in W1,p(Ω; R3), and rank DF0 = rank Df almost everywhere on K. 3. The compact set F0(K) is contained in finitely many compact flat plate patches with pairwise disjoint ambient neighborhoods. Each patch lies in a plane of slope at most Cλ in one of the chosen coordinates. Each patch has an assigned rank, either one or two; the rank-one patches can in addition retain any prescribed small directional grouping of im Df. 4. There is a compact zero-volume set Z ⋐ Λ, contained in finitely many piecewise affine graph sheets, such that S0 : Λ \ S−1 0 (Z) −→ Λ \ Z (2.8) 12 is a locally bi-Lipschitz homeomorphism. Its only non-singleton fibres are the collapsed vertical intervals over points of Z. Consequently F0 is a homeomorphism from Ω \ F−1 0 (Z) onto Λ \ Z. For almost every target point outside Z, its unique preimage under this last homeomorphism either is a regular point of F0 with positive invertible differential and the power-mean test in (2.1), or belongs to a fixed source null set. When p ≥ 3, the second alternative occurs only on a target null set.

candidates.label: Proposition 2.13
candidates.name: Two-round exact carrier
candidates.heading: Proposition 2.13 (Two-round exact carrier).
candidates.statement: Prescribe a positive continuous source value tolerance a : Ω → (0, ∞) before applying Proposition 2.6. Use there a target tolerance aΛ satisfying aΛ(y) ≤ 1 4a(f−1 (y)), and then fix the resulting rank data and endpoint protections of Lemma 2.7. Fix also an enlargement factor A > 1 for the marked collars, before assigning their facet budgets, and let ε > 0. After a total µ-loss smaller than ε, a first round of choices gives κ > 0, a compact retained source set K, a continuous proper onto carrier F1 b : Ω → Λ, an exact open target set O1, and compact endpoint rectangles strictly inside O1. These choices precede any prescribed residual-volume thresholds. Fix a locally finite target Whitney tiling Q, and choose arbitrary numbers aQ > 0 for Q ∈ Q, after O1 and the endpoint buffers have been determined. A second round gives Fb : Ω → Λ and O ⊃ O1 such that: (i) Fb is continuous, proper and onto, belongs to W1,p loc , and has only the countable tame ball fibres of Lemma 2.10. It is a genuine homeomorphism on target neighborhoods away from their values and accumulation seams. For p ≥ 3 it satisfies volume Lusin N. (ii) O is a locally finite union of exact affine or PL core images. Every compact subset of such a core has a neighborhood on which Fb and its inverse are exactly those of its affine or PL chart. In particular no point of O has a nontrivial fibre, and L3 (Q \ O) < aQ (Q ∈ Q). (2.29) The compact endpoint rectangles retain their fixed buffers in O1. (iii) Fb = Fκ on a neighborhood of K. It meets the prescribed fine value tolerance relative to f. The choices of κ and of the retained central margins ensure that Fκ(K) stays in the protected central plate neighborhoods. (iv) When 2 < p < 3, there is a locally finite family of marked source cubes U with disjoint closures, away from K, such that Z S U (1 + |Df|p ) < ε. (2.30) For p ≥ 3 this family is empty. Off the marked cubes the energy has the universal buffered regional estimate described below. (v) Write CU (w) for a cube-radius collar of physical width w about ∂U. For the prescribed enlargement factor A, the widths wU > 0 can be chosen after both rounds, with disjoint enlarged marked cubes, so that X U ℓU wU Z CU (AwU ) |DFb|p < ε. (2.31) The same bound, multiplied by the pth power of the Lipschitz constant, holds after a uniformly Lipschitz output composition. The enlarged cubes may still have original (1 + |Df|p)-mass less than 2ε. 27 The regional estimate in (iv) has the following meaning. Suppose a locally finite family of regional tests Aj and two successive small open buffered enlargements A [1] j and A [2] j are prescribed before the implants are made. All implants may be chosen so fine that Z Aj\ S U |DFb|p ≤ Cp Z A [2] j |Df|p for every j. (2.32) Here each enlargement has positive local buffer, the supports and comparison boxes meeting Aj fit inside its first enlargement at the corresponding round, and Cp is independent of all selected jet condition numbers, residual thresholds, and PL reference-map constants. In particular the tests may be reserved full-rank cut shells or ordinary regions outside prescribed interiors. The same construction works for summably weighted such tests toward the ends of the open domains.

candidates.label: Proposition 2.16
candidates.name: Postponed full-rank correction
candidates.heading: Proposition 2.16 (Postponed full-rank correction).
candidates.statement: Let p > 2 and let f : Ω → Λ be an orientation- preserving Sobolev homeomorphism between bounded domains. Let R be the set of its regular differentiation points at which Df has rank three. Let P ⋐ Ω be any previously protected compact set disjoint from R. Given ε > 0, one can choose finitely many pairwise disjoint buffered source cubes, disjoint from P, with centers xj ∈ R, radii rj, and positive affine jets Aj = Df(xj), bj(x) = f(xj) + Aj(x − xj), such that the inner cubes Kj = xj + rjB satisfy Z R\ S j Kj |Df|p < ε, X j Z Kj |Df − Aj|p < ε. (2.36) Their buffered cutoff bands Ej = {xj + rjξ : |t(ξ)| ≤ Cs} can have arbitrarily small total f-energy, even after multiplication by all the finitely bounded affine factors Cp|Aj|p|A−1 j |p. On those bands the normalized f is within cs/4 of the identity. Write Qj = xj + rjB(C+1)s for the buffered outer cubes. After these choices there are numbers vj > 0 and β > 0 such that every smooth diffeomorphism k : Ω → Λ satisfying sup Qj |k − f| < vj for each j, X j Z Ej |Dk|p < β can be changed only inside the associated outer cubes xj + rjB2s to a locally bi-Lipschitz homeomor- phism e k : Ω → Λ with e k = bj on Kj. The sum of the derivative-error integrals on the inner cubes and their modified shells is less than ε, after starting the selection with smaller error prescriptions if necessary. The cubes and tests may also be chosen to retain any prescribed positive continuous value tolerance for the final modification. A locally bi-Lipschitz preliminary map in W1,p(Ω; R3) can be used in place of k by first applying Theorem A.1, preserving the finite value and band-energy tests with room to spare.

candidates.label: Proposition 3.3
candidates.name: A proper product quantizer
candidates.heading: Proposition 3.3 (A proper product quantizer).
candidates.statement: Fix 0 < c < m with c < 1. One can choose a locally finite family of interior sites in Λ, with one contact at each ordinary site and the two protected 39 contacts at each paired site. The family can include the rectangular paired arrays constructed in Lemma 3.4. Index these site and contact pairs by i, writing them as (qi, xi), and define G(q) = sup i {F(qi) + xi · (q − qi) + c 2|q − qi|2 }, T = (∂G)−1 , (3.4) where the supremum also includes the support based at every qi / ∈ Λ. Here q is an output of T, and y ∈ ∂G(q) is an input. Then T : R3 → R3 is single-valued and c−1-Lipschitz, equals the identity outside Λ, and restricts to a proper onto map of Λ to itself, as finely close to the identity as prescribed. Inside Λ, G − c|q|2/2 is a locally finite maximum of affine functions. Its diagram has compact convex polyhedral cells. Write pi = xi − cqi. Over the relative interior of a face P, whose active indices are I(P), its exact input product is ∂G(q) = cq + conv{pi : i ∈ I(P)}, T(cq + v) = q (q ∈ relint P). (3.5) The two factors have orthogonal direction spaces of complementary dimensions. Every retained support owns a genuine three-dimensional output cell Ci. Its closed input block Xi = cCi + pi (3.6) is compactly contained in O. These closed blocks are pairwise disjoint and have locally finite, mutually disjoint protective neighborhoods within the exact regions of the carrier. Outside their union the output of T lies in the two-skeleton of the diagram.

candidates.label: Proposition 3.8
candidates.name: The graph exterior and its two colours
candidates.heading: Proposition 3.8 (The graph exterior and its two colours).
candidates.statement: Choose a small ru,D > 0 in every subcell. In input target coordinates remove the full closed blocks Xi and the open cores of the interval prisms over dD +ru,D(D −dD), with their ends attached to the full blocks. The closure My of the remainder is a locally finite PL three-manifold with boundary. The radial projection in each subcell, identity on subedges, defines a continuous map πT : My −→ Γ, where Γ is the subedge graph. Each component of My is a possibly noncompact graph handlebody. In particular every PL embedded compact interior two-sphere bounds a PL ball and H2(My; Z) = 0. (3.12) For intermediate levels there are two standard families of proper walls: AD(t) is the perimeter at common radial label t, times the face-offset interval; Be(s) is the entire inverse of the intermediate subedge point under πT. Walls within one colour are disjoint. Each A is an incompressible annulus and each B is a disk. An incident pair has two boundary intersection points, one on each annular end; a nonincident pair has none. Consequently transverse individually standard walls with this boundary incidence have one spanning intersection arc for each incident pair, and otherwise only circles; every such circle is contractible in both walls.

candidates.label: Proposition 4.3
candidates.name: Routing and good parameters
candidates.heading: Proposition 4.3 (Routing and good parameters).
candidates.statement: For every pre-stack root j, outside a null subset of (0, wj), the diagonal rule constructs a connected, oriented, properly embedded surface Lj,λ whose boundary, with coorientation, is the prescribed boundary of the original j-level at parameter λ. Different constructed surfaces are disjoint except for the prescribed essential arc intersections between opposite-colour roots. Each such surface is obtained by attaching punctured disks and annuli along a rooted tree; it may have ends at infinity. The following stronger local finiteness holds for each constructed surface: for every compact K ⊂ Mx, only finitely many of its reached states have an original parent collar meeting K.

candidates.label: Proposition 4.5
candidates.name: Conservation of oriented periods
candidates.heading: Proposition 4.5 (Conservation of oriented periods).
candidates.statement: Let L = Lj,λ be a good routed surface. Let Wj,λ ⊂ Mx be the pullback by h∗ of the standard cut at the exact affine label corresponding to λ ∈ (0, wj). Give both surfaces the coorientation of increasing standard parameter. For every compact path γ with endpoints on ∂Mx \ ∂L, their relative oriented intersection numbers agree: I(γ, L) = I(γ, Wj,λ). (4.4) Here intersection numbers may be defined after general-position perturbation relative to the endpoints. If the original path has finitely many hits on L, its signed local crossings give the same number and |I(γ, L)| ≤ #(γ ∩ L), where hits are counted with their occurrences along the path.

candidates.label: Proposition 4.9
candidates.name: Guard barrier
candidates.heading: Proposition 4.9 (Guard barrier).
candidates.statement: Fix the data of Definition 4.6, the capacities Ca and a positive continuous local layer-support accuracy. There are sufficiently fine net spacings and sufficiently small approximation and stair errors, depending only on these prior data, with the following property. If a pre-stack system satisfies (4.7) and avoids the resulting guards, then every point of every good routed layer is within the prescribed local accuracy, under q∗, of that layer’s standard physical support.

candidates.label: Theorem 4.11
candidates.name: Conditional wall realization
candidates.heading: Theorem 4.11 (Conditional wall realization).
candidates.statement: Fix the quantizer, carrier, exterior and boundary data above. Fix 0 < ζ < 1, c∗ > 0, the requested locally positive label and value accuracies, and locally finite buffered charts with finite capacities Ca. Choose guards and feature-stair accuracies in the order of Definition 4.6 and Proposition 4.9. Suppose the resulting sampled pre-stacks satisfy Definition 4.2, avoid these guards, and admit a slope majorant G obeying the previously fixed capacities (4.7). The sample intervals are ordered, have the affine parametrizations pj, and satisfy the slot, gap and accuracy choices of Lemma 4.1. Then there are finite unions of occupied closed intervals Ej satisfying (4.1) and a locally bi- Lipschitz homeomorphism h : Mx −→ My, h|∂Mx = h∗|∂Mx , which sends every occupied routed layer at parameter λ to the standard layer at label pj(λ), with the same affine parametrization on all occupied components. It extends by the prescribed h∗ on the removed cores and tubes. Moreover qh = Th is as finely close to q∗ on Mx as prescribed. The Theorem uses only the preassigned capacities for its choice of guards. Existence of a system meeting its hypotheses at that resolution is the separate content of Proposition 6.10, Lemma 7.3, and Proposition 7.4.

candidates.label: Proposition 4.12
candidates.name: Parameter cost after realization
candidates.heading: Proposition 4.12 (Parameter cost after realization).
candidates.statement: On occupied pre-stack pieces, a final active root parameter has local differential ±duj. On a routed circle box it has local differential ±d(wj − uj + uk) = ±(−duj + duk), (4.17) with the local coordinate reversals understood. At such a switched point only one root scalar is active. At an essential box both original root scalars persist independently. Consequently the exterior derivative costs of P0Th depend on these parameter differentials and the speeds in (4.15), with no factor involving Dh or the number of switches.

candidates.label: Proposition 4.13
candidates.name: Strict target compositions
candidates.heading: Proposition 4.13 (Strict target compositions).
candidates.statement: For a fixed realization h as above, the singular composition P0Th admits locally bi-Lipschitz homeomorphic approximations PεTηh with arbitrarily small prescribed local W1,p differences and value errors. Prescriptions may be summable on a compact exhaustion. Only local finiteness of the uncontrolled strict derivatives is required in regions whose energy is subsequently removed by a source collapse.

candidates.label: Proposition 5.6
candidates.name: Normalization with individual edge bounds
candidates.heading: Proposition 5.6 (Normalization with individual edge bounds).
candidates.statement: Let M be an orientable irreducible PL three-manifold with a locally finite triangulation. Let (Sj) be a locally finite family of pairwise disjoint, compact, properly embedded PL surfaces in general position. Each Sj is a disk or an annulus; in the annulus case its core is noncontractible in M. Assume that the prescribed boundary traces are straight normal arcs in boundary triangles and that #(Sj ∩ e) ≤ 1 for every boundary edge e and every j. Then there is a locally finite disjoint family (S′ j) with the same individual topologies, coorientations, and exact boundary traces, consisting of normal triangles and quadrilaterals, such that #(S′ j ∩ e) ≤ #(Sj ∩ e) for every j and every edge e. For a finite family the replacements can be obtained by an ambient isotopy relative to the boundary. Consequently any initially prescribed upper bounds on the individual edge counts are retained. This assertion concerns one colour only; it imposes no requirement to preserve the other colour.

candidates.label: Proposition 6.9
candidates.name: Sharp-island geometric contract
candidates.heading: Proposition 6.9 (Sharp-island geometric contract).
candidates.statement: Fix η, the compact chart and basis bounds, and the finite template choices above. The calibrated islands admit pre-stacks with all the qualitative properties of Definition 4.2 and with the following quantitative properties. 1. Throughout an enlarged equal-weight island the pre-slope density is at most CMσ in aligned units. This constant is independent of microscopic master widths, central crossing angles, final guard gaps, H, W, and the final level-count tolerance δ′. 2. In deep regular low-leakage portions, the scalar gradients obey (6.6). At concurrent independent strips the two-coordinate squared Frobenius cost is at most 2 + Cη. At an occupied diagonal transition after routing, the active coordinate has gradient ±∇uj ± ∇uk, whose squared norm has the same bound. In parallel mode the opponent bands are disjoint in these portions and the squared norm is at most 1 + Cη. Occupied-stair speeds multiply these bounds by at most (1 + Cζ)2. 3. In a regular tetrahedron the excluded CNW neighborhoods of its faces, all its main slab creases, and its non-slab disks occupy relative volume at most CN  W H + δ′  . (6.9) The canonical protection and broadening margins only change the fixed factor CN . Nonregular tetrahedra, high-leakage tetrahedra, their required fixed-neighbor layers, and patch boundary margins are charged by their full Mp-cost. The norm statements concern the smooth compatible label sectors after the combined label barrier, away from central radial activation cutoffs. They are geometric scalar-pair estimates; their physical conversion and the saturation argument are made in Lemma 7.6.

candidates.label: Proposition 6.10
candidates.name: Geometric realization of pre-stacks
candidates.heading: Proposition 6.10 (Geometric realization of pre-stacks).
candidates.statement: Suppose the central starting systems have the boundary data of Lemma 5.2 and the wall-by-wall edge upper counts used in the separate- colour normalization of Proposition 5.6. Suppose also that the weighted edge tests have been selected as in Lemma 5.3. The constructions of Sections 5 and 6 give the pre-stacks required in Definition 4.2: same-colour compact disjoint collars; opposite arc or circle products with the full parameter rectangles; individual pattern trivializations preserving the opposite parameter; the exact boundary correspondence; and locally bi-Lipschitz changed coordinates in which the relevant endpoint arrangements and parameters are PL. Their pre-parameter slopes admit a density G satisfying the ordinary bound (5.6), the fixed boundary and chart bounds of Lemma 5.2, and the island bound G ≤ CMσ of Proposition 6.9. All constants in these inequalities may be fixed before choosing final guard gaps, mesh resolutions, and sample weights. Consequently any crude compact-local integral capacities deduced from these inequalities and the conditional edge-variation bounds are independent of those later choices. The actual simultaneous choice of the capacities, meshes, and samples is supplied by Lemma 7.3 and Proposition 7.4.

candidates.label: Proposition 7.4

candidates.heading: Proposition 7.4 (Initial walls with the selected budgets).
candidates.statement: The guards, mesh, samples and count bounds selected in Lemma 7.3 admit pre-stacks satisfying Definition 4.2 and avoiding the selected guards. Their actual slope majorant G satisfies Z Uj Gp ≤ Aj on every buffered barrier chart Uj, together with the weak and sharp estimates of Lemmas 7.1 and 7.2. The mesh and samples are unchanged. Consequently the hypotheses of Theorem 4.11 hold.

candidates.statement: Let Ω, Ω′ ⊂ R3 be bounded domains, let 1 ≤ p < ∞, and let H : Ω → Ω′ be a locally bi-Lipschitz homeomorphism in W1,p(Ω; R3). (A.1) In particular, g belongs to W1,p(Ω; R3), and the approximations have exactly the target Ω′.

candidates.label: Theorem 1.1

This construction uses a zero joint-blank digit, so every initial tape coordinate is a finite radix sum. Its temporal alternative belongs to L2(0, ∞; Hj) for every j.

candidates.label: Proposition 13.5
candidates.name: Full solid boxes with a height guard
candidates.heading: Proposition 13.5 (Full solid boxes with a height guard).
candidates.statement: Let the source and target families be finite collections of full rational axis-aligned solid boxes, each family pairwise disjoint. Write their centers as ai, bi and their positive half-widths as ri,j, wi,j. Require each prescribed affine map to send its entire source box onto its specified target box: Fi(ai + h) = bi + Dih, Di = diag(wi,1/ri,1, wi,2/ri,2, wi,3/ri,3), det Di = 1. Suppose every source center has height at most −1, and every target center has height at most −1 or exactly 1. They admit an effective compactly supported solenoidal unit-time realization. If a target center has negative height, every point ai + h of its source box with h3 = 0 remains at negative height throughout. A rational bound for the entire support is computable from the boxes.

candidates.label: Theorem 13.6
candidates.name: A height test inside one torus chart
candidates.heading: Theorem 13.6 (A height test inside one torus chart).
candidates.statement: On the unit torus, the fixed label o = (1/2, 1/2, 1/2) and event {x : x3 (mod 1) ∈ (1/2, 1)} (45) realize halting by a smooth general mean-zero force, periodic after time one, with zero initial velocity and pressure and bounded mixed derivatives. The repeated mechanism depends on the machine alone; only initialization depends on its finite input. The solution is unique in the torus class.

candidates.label: Proposition 13.7
candidates.name: Column and layer transport
candidates.heading: Proposition 13.7 (Column and layer transport).
candidates.statement: Let Si, Ti be finite rational planar rectangle families of positive side lengths, each separately disjoint, with endpoints on the B−2 grid, where B ≥ 2 is an integer. Let their assigned center-to-center positive reciprocal diagonal affine maps satisfy Fi(Si) = Ti. A finite effective solenoidal field in R3 realizes all these maps on the rectangles in z = 0. Along each tracked path the first coordinate stays between its initial and final values. The field has compact support and flat time collars.

candidates.label: Theorem 13.8
candidates.name: A half-space test by fixed columns
candidates.heading: Theorem 13.8 (A half-space test by fixed columns).
candidates.statement: On R3, the frontier recorder with odd digits in base 2m + 1 realizes halting from the fixed label 0 by the event x1 < −1. It gives a compactly supported general force, periodic after time one, with zero initial velocity and pressure and all mixed derivatives bounded.

candidates.label: Theorem 13.9
candidates.name: The delayed-head column realization
candidates.heading: Theorem 13.9 (The delayed-head column realization).
candidates.statement: The table of Lemma 5.3 has a realization on R3 with fixed label 0 and detector x1 < −1, compact spatial support, period one after time one, bounded mixed derivatives and uniformly bounded kinetic energy. The prescribed pressure is zero. Uniqueness holds in the whole-space comparison class, in particular when the competitor and its first spatial derivatives are bounded on every finite time interval.

candidates.label: Theorem 13.10
candidates.name: A fixed box test with recorded pointers
candidates.heading: Theorem 13.10 (A fixed box test with recorded pointers).
candidates.statement: On R3, the fixed label (2, 0, 0) and open box (0, 1)2 × (−1/2, 1/2) realize halting by an effective general force with compact spatial support, zero initial velocity and pressure, bounded mixed derivatives, and period one after time one. The construction moves whole solid boxes. Uniqueness holds among smooth competitors with u ∈ C1 ([0, T]; L2 ), ∇u, ∆u ∈ C([0, T]; L2 ), p, ∇p ∈ C([0, T]; L2 ), sup [0,T]×R3 (|u| + |∇u|) < ∞ for every finite T.

candidates.label: Theorem 13.11
candidates.name: A guarded planar observation with unrestricted pressure
candidates.heading: Theorem 13.11 (A guarded planar observation with unrestricted pressure).
candidates.statement: On R3, the fixed label (−4, 0, 0) and fixed box (−1, 2)2 × (−1, 1) realize halting by a compactly supported general force with zero initial velocity and prescribed pressure and all mixed derivatives bounded. One choice is periodic after time one. A separate choice satisfies ∥f(t)∥∞ = O((1 + t)−2/3) and f ∈ L2([0, ∞) × R3). Uniqueness holds among smooth competitors with u ∈ C([0, T]; H2) ∩ C1([0, T]; L2) and bounded u, ∇u on each finite interval, without any spatial integrability condition on pressure. Pressure is unique modulo a function of time.

candidates.label: Proposition 14.1
candidates.name: Linear scaling into the torus
candidates.heading: Proposition 14.1 (Linear scaling into the torus).
candidates.statement: The direction recorder without its passive track has a unit-torus realization periodic after t = 1, with fixed label (1/8, 0, 0) and halting event x1 ∈ (−1/4, 0) (mod 1). Each period acts on full solid boxes; the pressure is zero and the force has zero mean.

candidates.label: Proposition 14.2
candidates.name: Exponential deformation in a fixed chart
candidates.heading: Proposition 14.2 (Exponential deformation in a fixed chart).
candidates.statement: The move-first recorder has a unit-torus realization periodic after one loading interval, with fixed label (1/4, 1/4, 1/4) and halting event x1 ∈ (2/3, 5/6) (mod 1). The repeated motion acts on thickened closed rectangles and their neighborhoods. Its mean-zero residual has the form f0 + νf1 with coefficients independent of ν.

candidates.label: Theorem 14.3
candidates.name: A direct unit-cube implementation
candidates.heading: Theorem 14.3 (A direct unit-cube implementation).
candidates.statement: At each fixed positive computable viscosity, every machine and finite input has an effective smooth mean-zero force on the unit flat three-torus, with bounded mixed derivatives and period one for t ≥ 1, whose smooth zero-data solution satisfies ∃t ≥ 0 : X(t; (1/4, 1/4, 1/4)) ∈ (2/3, 5/6) × T2 ⇐⇒ the machine halts. The normalized pressure is zero and the solution is unique in the classical torus comparison class of Section 2.

candidates.label: Theorem 14.4
candidates.name: A height-separated mechanism with an origin track
candidates.heading: Theorem 14.4 (A height-separated mechanism with an origin track).
candidates.statement: On the unit torus, the fixed label (1/8, 3/8, 1/4) and strip 2/3 < x1 < 7/8 realize halting by a smooth mean-zero general force, periodic after time one, with zero initial velocity and pressure and bounded mixed derivatives. A permanent tape track identifies the original absolute origin. For a fixed machine the repeated field is independent of the input.

candidates.label: Proposition 15.1
candidates.heading: Proposition 15.1.
candidates.statement: The template of Theorem 11.3 admits a force in L2([0, ∞) × R3) with the same material label and event. The template of Theorem 11.4 admits a force in L2([0, ∞); Hj(R3)) for every integer j ≥ 0. Both retain uniform compact support, zero initial velocity, bounded mixed derivatives, their stated pressure and velocity comparison classes, and finite effective prescriptions.

candidates.label: Corollary 15.2
candidates.name: Two profiles of the input-offset processor
candidates.heading: Corollary 15.2 (Two profiles of the input-offset processor).
candidates.statement: On T3, the fixed label P = (1/4, 1/4, 0) and strip O = {1/32 < Y < 1/8} realize halting from zero velocity by two effective mean-zero general forces. One is stationary after time one. The other tends to zero uniformly and has every mixed-derivative spatial supremum norm in L2(0, ∞). Both have bounded mixed derivatives, zero prescribed pressure, uniformly bounded kinetic energy, and uniqueness in the torus comparison class.

manuscripts.title: Uniform Interior $`C^{1,\alpha}`$ Estimates for Infinity-Harmonic Functions

candidates.label: Theorem 1.1
candidates.name: Uniform interior estimate
candidates.heading: Theorem 1.1 (Uniform interior estimate).
candidates.statement: For every integer d ≥ 3 there are constants αd ∈ (0, 1/3] and Cd < ∞ such that every bounded infinity-harmonic function u ∈ C(B1), where B1 ⊂ Rd, belongs to C1,αd (B1/2) and satisfies ∥∇u∥L∞(B1/2) + [∇u]C0,αd (B1/2) ≤ Cd oscB1 u.

candidates.label: Corollary 1.2
candidates.name: Interior C1 regularity
candidates.heading: Corollary 1.2 (Interior C1 regularity).
candidates.statement: Let d ≥ 3, let Ω ⊆ Rd be a nonempty connected open set, and let u ∈ C(Ω) be infinity-harmonic. Then u ∈ C1 loc(Ω).

candidates.label: Proposition 2.3
candidates.name: Affine blow-ups at a fixed center
candidates.heading: Proposition 2.3 (Affine blow-ups at a fixed center).
candidates.statement: Let w be infinity-harmonic in D and let z ∈ D. Every locally uniform limit, along a sequence ri ↓ 0, of Vi(Y ) = w(z + riY ) − w(z) ri is a linear function on Rn. Such limits exist after passage to subsequences.

candidates.label: Proposition 2.5
candidates.name: Three-point flatness
candidates.heading: Proposition 2.5 (Three-point flatness).
candidates.statement: Let Ui be infinity-harmonic on B1 ⊂ Rn with a common Lipschitz bound, and let ℓi be affine functions such that ∥Ui − ℓi∥L∞(B1) −→ 0. Then sup x,y∈B1/4 x̸=y |Ui(x) + Ui(y) − 2Ui((x + y)/2)| |x − y| −→ 0. (2.1)

candidates.label: Theorem 3.1
candidates.name: Liouville Theorem
candidates.heading: Theorem 3.1 (Liouville Theorem).
candidates.statement: Let m ≥ 1 and 0 ≤ C0 < ∞. Suppose that v ∈ C(Rm × R) is a viscosity solution of F[v] := D2 v[(∇xv, 1)] = 0. (3.1) Suppose, in addition, that for every z = (x, t) ∈ Rm × R and every R > 0 there are p ∈ Rm and a ∈ R such that v(x + h, t + ℓ) − v(x, t) − p · h − a − |p|2 2 ! ℓ ≤ C0R if |ℓ| ≤ R, |h − pℓ| ≤ R. (3.2) Then v is affine.

candidates.label: Proposition 3.3
candidates.name: Uniform power decay
candidates.heading: Proposition 3.3 (Uniform power decay).
candidates.statement: Assume Theorem 3.1. There are B ∈ (0, ∞), γ ∈ (0, 1], and s0 ∈ (0, 1/8], depending only on d, such that b(s) ≤ Bsγ (0 < s ≤ s0). (3.9)

candidates.label: Proposition 3.6
candidates.heading: Proposition 3.6.
candidates.statement: For the sequence supplied by Lemma 3.4 and the normalization (3.14), a subse- quence of the vi converges locally uniformly to a nonaffine function v ∈ C(Rd × R) satisfying (3.1) and (3.2) with one finite constant C0.

candidates.label: Corollary 5.3
candidates.name: A barycentric subsolution
candidates.heading: Corollary 5.3 (A barycentric subsolution).
candidates.statement: Let f ∈ C(Rm × (0, ∞)) be a viscosity subsolution of (3.1) with subquadratic spatial growth on compact time intervals. Then (x, t) 7→ Ctf(x, t) is a viscosity subsolution of (3.1) on Rm × (0, ∞). For every c ∈ R, the same holds for (x, t) 7→ Ctf(x, t) − ct.

candidates.label: Proposition 5.4
candidates.name: Extremal envelope contact
candidates.heading: Proposition 5.4 (Extremal envelope contact).
candidates.statement: If Am,C0 contains a nonaffine member, then there exist κ ∈ (0, ∞) and v ∈ Am,C0 centered at z∗ = (0, 1) for which (5.2) holds with f = v and I = R. For t > 0 set W(x, t) = Ctv(x, t) − κ2t 2 . (5.7) This function is continuous, has subquadratic spatial growth on compact positive-time intervals, and is a viscosity subsolution of (3.1) on Rm × (0, ∞). It satisfies v(x, t) − κ2t 2 ≤ W(x, t) ≤ v(x, t) (t > 0), W(z∗) = v(z∗) = 0, (5.8) and W(·, t)−|x|2/(2t) is concave for every t > 0. At every point of contact with t > 0, the barycentric gap satisfies W(x, t) = v(x, t) =⇒ Ctv(x, t) − v(x, t) t = κ2 2 > 0. (5.9) Finally, Hv(z∗) ∈ R, lim ℓ↓0 S+ ℓ W(z∗) = Hv(z∗). (5.10)

candidates.label: Proposition 7.1
candidates.heading: Proposition 7.1.
candidates.statement: Put δj = 2−j for j ≥ 1. There exist a constant K < ∞, a point xend ∈ Rm, and an infinite set J ⊂ N with the following property. For every j ∈ J there are a point xj ∈ Rm and a fit (pj, aj) for v at (xj, δj) of radius δj, in the sense of (3.2), such that Hv(xend, 0) > −∞, W(xj, δj) = v(xj, δj), |xend − xj + pjδj| ≤ Kδj. (7.1)
